note: Original language puzzles. Stars show how independently a puzzle was solved; they are not a language level or score.

puzzles.title: Walk to School
puzzles.prompt: Tap the words to build a sentence that tells how you get to school.
hints: Start with the word that names who is walking.
A verb comes right after the speaker. Which tile tells what the speaker does?
Two sentences work: you can put "every day" at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: The Sleeping Dog
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about where the dog is.
hints: The word "the" appears twice. One starts the sentence.
Say who it is about first, then "is sleeping".
A place phrase comes last: under + the + table.

puzzles.title: Lunch Question
puzzles.prompt: Build a question that asks about lunch.
hints: Questions with "where" often start with the question word.
After the question word comes a helper word: do.
Then the speaker, the action, and the thing: you eat lunch.

puzzles.title: Stay Inside
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that gives a reason. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: The word "because" starts the reason part.
The reason part is: it was raining. The result part is: we stayed inside.
Put the result first or the reason first. Both are correct.

puzzles.title: Spring Garden
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about planting. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Find the people: my brother and I.
Then the action and the thing: plant tomatoes.
"In spring" tells when. It can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: Although the Test
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that shows a contrast. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Although" begins the part that is surprising.
The "although" part is: the test was difficult. The main part is: most students finished early.
You can put the "although" part first or last.

puzzles.title: Volcano Scientists
puzzles.prompt: Build one sentence that tells which scientists wear special helmets.
hints: The word "who" connects a group of people to a description of them.
The group is "scientists". The description is "who study volcanoes".
After the description comes the main action: wear special helmets.

puzzles.title: Ancient Builders
puzzles.prompt: Build a question about how ancient builders worked.
hints: Start with the question word that asks about the way something was done.
After the question word comes a helper in the past: did. Then the subject.
"Such heavy stones" ends the question. Which describing word comes before "stones"?

puzzles.title: Who Has Which Pet?
puzzles.prompt: Match each friend to a pet. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: pet

clues.text: Ana's pet lives in a bowl of water.
Ben's pet is not the cat.

hints: Start with the clue that tells you exactly one match.
Ana's pet lives in water, so it is the fish. Cross the fish off for Ben and Cy.
Ben's pet is not the cat, and the fish is taken. What is left for Ben?

puzzles.title: Lunch Drinks
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to a drink. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: drink

clues.text: Mia does not drink milk or juice.
Leo drinks either milk or water.

hints: "Does not drink milk or juice" means Mia drinks neither one.
If Mia drinks neither milk nor juice, only one drink is left for her.
Mia has the water. Leo drinks either milk or water, so which one can he have?

puzzles.title: Music Club
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to an instrument. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: instrument

clues.text: Sam does not play the piano.
Sam does not play the violin.
Rita plays either the violin or the drums.

hints: Start with the two clues about Sam. They leave only one instrument.
Sam does not play the piano or the violin, so Sam plays the drums.
Rita plays either the violin or the drums. The drums are taken, so which does she play, and what is left for Tom?

puzzles.title: After-School Activities
puzzles.prompt: Match four friends to four activities. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: activity

clues.text: Ava does not do soccer or chess.
Cara does not do art, band, or chess.

hints: Look for the clue that rules out three activities for one person.
Cara does not do art, band, or chess, so Cara does soccer. Nobody else can do soccer.
Ava does not do soccer, chess, or band, so she does art. Dev cannot do band, so what can Dev do? Then Ben gets the last one.

puzzles.title: Favorite Subjects
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to their favorite subjects. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: favorite subject

clues.text: Neither Elena nor Farid likes math best.
Grace likes either science or history best.
Farid does not like art best.
Grace does not like history best.

hints: Ask: who is allowed to like math best? Check each clue about math.
Elena and Farid cannot, and Grace likes science or history. So Hiro likes math.
With math taken, who can like art? Then use the last clue to decide Grace and Farid.

puzzles.title: Which Word Does Not Belong?
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Cat, dog, and rabbit are animals. A table is furniture.
hints: Say each word aloud. Is there a group of three?
Three of these words name living things.
Which word does not name a living thing?

puzzles.title: Action or Feeling?
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Run, jump, and swim are actions you can do with your body. Happy describes a feeling.
hints: Think about what each word tells you.
Three of these words are things you can do with your body.
Which word tells how someone feels instead of what they do?

puzzles.title: On the Calendar
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Monday, Friday, and Sunday are days of the week. July is a month.
hints: All four words are about time.
Three of them name a short part of a week.
Which word names a longer part of the year?

puzzles.title: Words About the Past
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Ancient, old, and historic describe things from the past. Modern describes the present or recent time.
hints: Think about the time each word points to.
Three words point back to a time long ago.
Which word points to now instead of long ago?

puzzles.title: Connecting Words
puzzles.prompt: Three connecting words do the same job. Find the one that does a different job.
puzzles.rule: In these sentences, because, since, and as give a reason. Although shows a contrast.
hints: Make a short sentence with each word. What job does it do?
Three of the words answer the question "why?".
Which word shows two ideas that seem to go against each other?

puzzles.title: Words for Persuading
puzzles.prompt: Three words have similar meanings. Find the one with a different meaning.
puzzles.rule: Persuade, convince, and urge are about trying to change what someone thinks or does. Ignore means to pay no attention.
hints: Think about what a speaker is doing with each word.
Three words are about talking to someone to change their mind.
Which word means paying no attention at all?
